questions.question: If three faces are visible in a view, and none of them are opposite pairs (which is guaranteed, since opposite faces never appear together), what must be true about the three hidden faces?
options: They are unrelated to the visible faces
They include the three faces opposite to the ones visible, since each visible face's opposite must be hidden
They are always blank
They cannot be determined at all
questions.rationale: Since each visible face's opposite can never also be visible, the opposite of every visible face must be among the three hidden faces.

questions.question: What does 'corner compatibility' check for when combining known face relationships?
options: Whether the die is a perfect cube physically
Whether a proposed set of three mutually adjacent faces could actually meet validly at a real corner of the cube
The die's total surface area
Whether the die has any color at all
questions.rationale: Corner compatibility verifies that a proposed trio of faces could genuinely all meet together at one of the cube's actual corners, given the known adjacency and opposite relationships.

questions.question: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have in total?
questions.rationale: A cube has 8 vertices (corners), each where exactly 3 faces meet.

questions.question: What does the 'eight vertex combinations' heading likely refer to?
options: Eight unrelated random face pairs
The eight distinct sets of three mutually adjacent faces, one for each corner of the cube
Eight different possible die colors
Eight different numbering systems for dice
questions.rationale: Since a cube has 8 corners, and each corner is where a unique set of 3 mutually adjacent faces meet, there are 8 such valid three-face corner combinations.

questions.question: What is a 'dice net'?
options: A net used to physically catch a rolling die
A 2D unfolded layout of a cube's six faces that can be folded up to form the 3D die
A grid used only for counting figures
A type of dice game
questions.rationale: A dice net is a flat, 2D arrangement of the cube's six faces that, when folded along the shared edges, forms the complete 3D die.

questions.question: What does the 'net opposite rule' help identify in an unfolded dice net?
options: Which faces are the same color
Which two faces in the flat net layout will become opposite faces once the net is folded into a cube
The total area of the net
Which face is the largest
questions.rationale: The net opposite rule identifies which pairs of faces, based on their positions in the flat unfolded layout, will end up opposite each other once the net is folded into a cube.

questions.question: What is the recommended 'mental method' for folding a net without physically constructing it?
options: Guessing the final arrangement randomly
Mentally tracking how each face moves and which edges meet as you imagine folding the net step by step
Ignoring the net entirely and using only views
Physically cutting out the net every time
questions.rationale: The mental folding method involves systematically imagining each fold step by step, tracking which edges come together and where each face ends up in the resulting cube.

questions.question: What makes a dice net 'invalid'?
options: It has exactly six squares
The flat layout cannot actually be folded into a proper cube without faces overlapping or leaving a gap
It uses letters instead of numbers
It is drawn in a different color
questions.rationale: An invalid net is one whose flat arrangement of six squares cannot actually fold into a complete, non-overlapping cube — not every arrangement of six squares is a valid cube net.

questions.question: In a standard cross-shaped dice net (one central square with four squares attached to its sides, plus one more attached to one of those), how are opposite faces typically positioned?
options: Directly adjacent to each other in the net
Opposite faces are usually separated by exactly one square in a straight line across the net
Opposite faces are always diagonal to each other
Opposite faces cannot be determined from a net
questions.rationale: In this common net layout, opposite faces are typically separated by exactly one square along a straight line of the net, once you know the standard folding pattern.

questions.question: Why is understanding dice nets useful for solving dice reasoning problems?
options: It has no practical use for solving problems
It provides an alternative, systematic way to determine opposite and adjacent face relationships without relying solely on 3D visualization
It only helps with drawing, not reasoning
It replaces the need to know the opposite-face rule
questions.rationale: Dice nets offer a systematic, 2D alternative for determining face relationships, which can be easier to reason about precisely than pure 3D mental visualization.
